text:
kai: FYI — at ~07:12 UTC we started seeing a surge of GPU attach failures in us-west2. Initial alert shows attach failures +50 in 5m. Correlating with local NVMe IOPS bursts on scratchpool nodes; looks like a cleanup/backscatter issue.

ops-bot: ALERT: gpu-attach-failures (us-west2) count=50 window=5m severity=high link=https://grafana/redwood/alerts/3456 :rotating_light:

dana: quick glance at dashboards — scratchpool iops jumped from ~2k to ~22k at 07:12, pattern is small write bursts consistent with mass-delete + scrub. Janitor pods show many concurrent sweeps.

maria: SMARTs on affected hosts show temperature rise (194 -> 205) and media retry uptick. Not yet hardware failures but increasing attach latency and retries.

ajay: likely cause = janitor/scrub concurrency colliding with attach waves. We saw this in load tests when many small-file deletes triggered cleaners. Short-term mitigations: throttle janitor concurrency in us-west2 and add fallback route for attaches to warm pool when local attach latency exceeds threshold. Proposed patch: 
```yaml
janitor:
  rate_limit_qps: "6"
  max_concurrency: "2"
  backoff_ms: "250"
```
Apply to a canary of 5 nodes first. Also add an attach circuit-breaker to route to warm-pool when attach > 400ms.

kai: patched canary (5 nodes) with rate_limit_qps=6 at 07:28. Attach failures dropped from 50 -> 4 over next 10m. Median attach latency improved from ~700ms to ~180ms. Janitor CPU climbed (because IO waiting decreased parallelism).

dana: good signal. We should avoid global throttle; instead we need a regional dynamic policy that samples local iops and temperature. Also reschedule heavy scrubs to off-peak — propose emergency shift for us-west2 scrubs to 03:00 UTC.

maria: host log snippet (host-gnode-42) at 07:12: 
```
[07:12:11] janitor: start sweep /scratch/tmp (concurrency=12)
[07:12:14] nvme: iops burst 22000, queue_depth=512
[07:12:45] gpu-attacher: attach timeout retry=1 host=gnode-42
```
This shows the backscatter: janitor starts, I/O queue backs up, attach times out.

ajay: action items: 1) roll regional throttle in us-west2 for 24h; 2) enable attach fallback to warm/dedicated pool; 3) add probe: if scratchpool_iops > 10k and attach_failures > 5 in 5m then trigger runbook. I'll open ticket INFRA-16233 and assign owners.

kai: enabling fallback in canary now — routing attaches to warm-pool when local attach > 400ms. Warm-pool absorbed load with small cost increase but prevented customer impact.

dana: follow-ups: - postmortem to analyze why janitor default concurrency = 12 in region; adjust heuristics to scale by observed iops not free-space. - telemetry: add backscatter_index metric = scrub_rw_bytes / attach_ops over sliding window.

maria: add alert scratchpool_backscatter_warning when backscatter_index > 0.8 and SMART temp > 200.

ajay: INFRA-16233 created, owners: kai (mitigation), dana (telemetry + schedule), maria (postmortem). Staged rollout plan: 10% -> 50% -> 100% over 2 hours.

ops-bot: ACTION_CREATED INFRA-16233 https://redwood/infra/tickets/16233 created by ajay assigned=[kai,dana,maria] priority=P1

kai: tl;dr — immediate mitigation worked (throttle + fallback). Next steps: telemetry + change janitor concurrency default. Will post postmortem after soak. :thumbsup:

maria: note on cost — warm-pool fallback estimated +4% monthly for affected tenants during event window, acceptable to avoid outages.

dana: scheduling controlled soak tomorrow 02:00 UTC, invite platform and oncall to monitor.

ajay: runbook tasks assigned. Closing loop; if regressions occur ping #eng-oncall and cc @kai.

(reactions: :white_check_mark: :wrench:)
